macro_blurb: Today's cross-Atlantic backdrop is shaped by trade and political headlines rather than central bank action: the EU and Mexico signed a trade agreement at a Latin America summit, supporting the external-demand narrative for European exporters, while Hungary's new opposition figure Magyar said Budapest will halt plans to withdraw from the International Criminal Court, easing one EU-internal friction point. In Washington, management churn in the Trump administration continues with intelligence chief Tulsi Gabbard resigning, and a federal judge dismissed charges against Kilmar Abrego Garcia, calling the prosecution "vindictive" — a reminder of ongoing legal-political noise around the DOJ. On the corporate side, two senior Walmart executives departed under new CEO John Furner (US retail), Qualcomm rallied on AI-device demand (US semis), and SpaceX completed a Starship test flight.
synthesis:
Today's screen is a value-and-yield grind, not a growth story. Average Value sits at the 84th percentile and Yield at 77th across the ten picks, with composites compressed in a narrow 75.3–88.9 band. Financial Services dominates at 3 of 10 (TROW, ALL, EG), Consumer Defensive contributes 2 (MO, KHC), and the regional split is lopsided: 9 US to 1 EU, despite the screen running across 539 scored names. Six of ten picks carry dividend yields above 5%, and five trade at single-digit trailing P/Es. This is a cash-return book assembled from unloved corners of the US market.

The clearest thread runs through the insurance and asset-management value trade: ALL at 4.8x earnings with a 22.3% FCF yield, EG at 7.2x and 0.92x book throwing off 28.6% FCF yield, and TROW at 11.1x with a 5.1% dividend — three Financial Services names where the market is pricing capital-return skepticism rather than franchise decay. A second thread links HPQ, MO, and KHC as deep-value, high-yield US consumer/tech laggards (dividends of 5.48%, 5.75%, 6.80%); the macro tape — Trump-administration churn, DOJ noise, Qualcomm's AI-driven rally bypassing legacy hardware — explains why HPQ still screens at 9.6x despite a 38% three-month run.

ENG.MC is the outlier: the only EU name, the only Utility, and the highest composite at 88.9, riding a 100th-percentile momentum reading the rest of the book doesn't share. The conspicuous absence is Technology — 1 pick from a sector of that size, and it's HPQ, not an AI name. Industrials, Consumer Cyclical, Real Estate and Communication Services are entirely absent: this screen has no cyclical-recovery or rate-sensitive duration exposure. Two macro items to watch over the next fortnight: HPQ's upcoming Q2 print, which can unwind the 38% rally on any guide cut, and the EU-Mexico trade agreement's read-through for European external demand — the one channel that could pull more EU names into a screen currently 90% American.
